issues.legal_issue: A broadly worded statutory power to exempt land or buildings from planning controls is constitutionally valid when the statute’s policy and other provisions provide guidance for its exercise.
material_facts: The challenged provision allowed the government to exempt land or buildings from provisions of the planning legislation and its subordinate rules, subject to conditions.

The legislation’s stated purpose and its provisions established a policy of planned development and regulated land use and construction through planning authorities, development plans, and detailed development rules.
The challengers argued that the exemption power lacked limits and allowed arbitrary departures from the planning regime.
issues.conclusion: The exemption provision is valid because the statute’s preamble, objects, and other provisions provide clear policy and guidance, so the power is not unbridled or an excessive delegation of essential legislative function.
issues.legal_principle: A legislature may delegate implementation of its policy but may not abdicate its essential legislative function. Guidance for delegated power may be found in the statute’s express provisions, preamble, scheme, objects, or subject matter. A wide exemption power is valid if it must be exercised consistently with the statute’s policy. The Court relied on State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara, In re The Delhi Laws Act, Harishankar Bagla v. State of Madhya Pradesh, Sardar Inder Singh v. State of Rajasthan, P.J. Irani v. State of Madras, Registrar of Co-operative Societies v. K. Kunhambu, Premium Granites v. State of Tamil Nadu, and distinguished A.N. Parasuraman v. State of Tamil Nadu and Kunnathat Thathunni Moopil Nair v. State of Kerala, where the statutes lacked adequate policy or guidance.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_delegated_ex: A party challenges the constitutionality of a law because it delegates power to grant exemptions from statutory requirements.
predicates.statute_states_planning_policy: The statute states a policy of planned development and regulated land use.
predicates.other_statutory_provisions_guide_exercis: The statute’s other provisions and subordinate rules provide standards that guide how the exemption power is to be exercised.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns a delegated exemption power, and the law states a relevant policy with other provisions guiding the power, the exemption power is valid.

issues.legal_issue: Exemption orders that disregard the governing planning policy, are issued mechanically without reasons or conditions, and override planning decisions are arbitrary and unlawful.
material_facts: The government issued numerous exemption orders for buildings that violated development rules, including rules governing setbacks, floor space, parking, access, safety, and other construction requirements.
The orders followed an almost identical form, gave no reasons, imposed no conditions, and did not show consideration of the planning policy or effects on the public.
Some exemptions overrode prior refusals by the planning authority.
The government filed no counter-affidavit responding to the allegations about the orders.
issues.conclusion: The challenged exemption orders were arbitrary, illegal, and unsustainable, and the Court quashed them.
issues.legal_principle: A statutory authority exercising even a broad discretion must act reasonably within the statute’s purpose and remain subject to judicial review. An exemption under the planning law must further the policy of planned development, take account of effects on public safety, convenience, and health, and include reasons showing application of mind. The provision also requires the government to impose such conditions as it considers appropriate when granting an exemption.

rule.if: challenge_to_exemption_orders and orders_disregard_planning_standards and orders_lack_reasons and orders_lack_conditions

predicates.challenge_to_exemption_orders: A party asks a court to review government orders granting exemptions from planning controls.
predicates.orders_disregard_planning_standards: The government grants exemptions despite substantial violations of standards intended to regulate development and protect the public.
predicates.orders_lack_reasons: The exemption orders do not state reasons showing why the government exercised its discretion.
predicates.orders_lack_conditions: The exemption orders impose no conditions to control the consequences of the exemptions.

issues.definition: When challenged exemption orders disregard planning standards and contain neither reasons nor conditions, they are arbitrary and must be quashed.

issues.legal_issue: A one-time legislative scheme for regularizing specified pre-existing unauthorized development is valid when the legislature itself defines the policy and the essential terms of the scheme.
material_facts: An amending law created a one-time mechanism for exempting qualifying land or buildings developed before the scheme commenced.
The law provided for applications, regularization fees, prescribed application requirements, and deemed permission after an exemption order.
The scheme was introduced in response to widespread unauthorized development and the stated practical difficulties of demolishing all such structures.
The challengers argued that the scheme continued the excessive and public-interest-defeating exemption power found in the earlier provision.
issues.conclusion: The one-time regularization scheme is valid because it embodies the legislature’s own policy and leaves little discretion to the government.
issues.legal_principle: The legislature may itself enact a policy to regularize a defined class of existing development and prescribe the mechanism for doing so. Such a legislative scheme is not invalid as an unguided delegation where the legislature states the policy and sets out the scheme’s essential requirements. The Court considered the scheme’s text and statement of objects and reasons and distinguished the broad discretionary exemption power under the earlier provision.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_one_time_reg: A party challenges the constitutionality of a law that creates a one-time process for regularizing existing development.
predicates.legislature_states_regularization_policy: The legislature expressly adopts a policy of regularizing a defined category of existing development.
predicates.legislature_defines_scheme_requirements: The legislature sets out the scheme’s eligibility, application, and payment requirements rather than leaving them to unrestricted executive choice.

issues.definition: When a challenged one-time regularization scheme reflects an express legislative policy and the legislature defines its requirements, the scheme is valid.

issues.legal_issue: The lack of individual public notice before decisions under a one-time regularization scheme does not invalidate the scheme where notice in every case is impracticable and an appeal mechanism is available.
material_facts: The scheme covered a very large number of developments made contrary to planning requirements before the scheme commenced.
The challengers argued that the public should receive notice because regularization could affect public rights and conveniences.
The law provided for an appeal against an order made under the scheme.
The Court considered public notice in every individual case impracticable for this one-time settlement and advised the State to consider providing public participation in future schemes.
issues.conclusion: The absence of individual public notice did not invalidate the one-time scheme, although the State should consider providing an opportunity for public objections in future schemes where public rights are affected.
issues.legal_principle: Whether individual public notice is required must be assessed in the context of the scheme and its practical operation. For a one-time settlement covering a very large number of cases, individual notice before each decision may not be practicable; an available appeal process is relevant. The Court also stated that future schemes should provide an opportunity for affected members of the public to raise objections, either at the initial stage or on appeal.

rule.if: challenge_to_regularization_without_public_notice and one_time_scheme_covers_many_cases and individual_notice_is_impracticable and appeal_mechanism_is_available

predicates.challenge_to_regularization_without_publ: A party argues that a regularization scheme is invalid because the public receives no individual notice before decisions are made.
predicates.one_time_scheme_covers_many_cases: The scheme is a one-time settlement applying to a large number of existing developments.
predicates.individual_notice_is_impracticable: Providing notice to the public in every individual case is impracticable in the circumstances.
predicates.appeal_mechanism_is_available: The scheme allows an appeal against a regularization decision.

issues.definition: When a challenged one-time scheme covers many cases, individual notice is impracticable, and an appeal is available, the absence of individual notice does not invalidate the scheme.

issues.legal_issue: Persons whose earlier exemptions are quashed may apply to have the resulting unauthorized development considered under an applicable regularization scheme.
material_facts: The Court quashed the exemption orders, which left the developments covered by those orders unauthorized.
A separate one-time regularization scheme and rules for processing applications were in force.
The people affected by the quashing could therefore seek regularization under that scheme.
The Court directed the government to publish notice inviting applications and directed the authorities to decide timely applications according to law.
issues.conclusion: The government must give the affected persons an opportunity to apply for regularization following public notice, and the competent authorities must decide their applications according to law.
issues.legal_principle: When quashing exemption orders leaves development unauthorized, an applicable statutory regularization process may provide a lawful route for affected persons to seek regularization. The Court directed that those persons be allowed to apply after public notice and that the authorities determine the applications under the governing scheme and rules.

predicates.exemption_orders_are_quashed: A court sets aside government orders that had exempted developments from planning requirements.
predicates.resulting_development_is_eligible_for_re: A regularization process applies to the development that remains unauthorized after the orders are set aside.

issues.definition: When exemption orders are quashed and the resulting unauthorized development falls within an available regularization process, the affected owners must be allowed to apply for regularization.
